acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Ira talks with comedian Rob Delany, who suffered the worst kind of loss a parent can endure — the death of his two-year-old son, Henry. Rob describes what his grief has been like and what he’s learned from it.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
Producer Chana Joffe-Walt wondered what it was like for surviving MTA employees coping with the loss of their co-workers due to Covid-19. She met one in particular who’s had a hard time saying goodbye.
Here's the memorial video the transit authority in New York City made to remember its workers who died from COVID.
acts.title: Goodbye Mr. Facey

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Producer Sean Cole has, unfortunately, experienced something known as “cumulative grief” this year. He writes about the multiple upheavals he’s been dealing with.
acts.title: When It Rains

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Producer Bim Adewunmi travels to the site in Minneapolis where George Floyd was murdered by a police officer. It’s become a huge, make-shift memorial, big enough to absorb the grief of all-comers who wish to pay homage.
acts.title: The Caretaker

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: One of the 590,000 casualties of U.S. Covid-19 this year was Leiah Danielle Jones. She was one of the “long haulers,” and she died in March 2021. But not before writing her own obituary.
acts.title: All My Love
